To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a white-light-emitting polymer diode with high efficiency and high luminance.
the phosphorescent dye Ir(CzBppf)2(PZ)(1) was used as a yellow dopant in a host polymer PFO(2) to produce a white light-emitting diode.

the white light emission is obtained from two emission bands in blue and yellow regions, and the white emission is achieved with the Ir(CzBppf)2(pZ) as dopant in PFO matrix, and the EL process in the WPLED is mainly the charge-trap mechanism, and the device exhibits a high efficiency and good stability of white light.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of a WPLED based on a phosphorescent Ir(CzBPF)2(PZ):PFO system.
a new approach to fabricate efficient WPLEDs with a phosphorescence dopant.
the development of a new type of WPLEDs with an efficient phosphorescent yellow dopant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the white light emission from the WPLED is due to the combination of the blue emission of the host PFO and the yellow emission of the Ir(CzBppf)2(PZ).
the device has a stable white emission with high efficiency and brightness.
the phosphorescent dopants can be used as a promising alternative to conventional fluorescent dopants for WPLEDs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new phosphorescent Ir complex, Ir(CzBPF)2(PZ)(2), has been successfully synthesized.
the WPLEDs with an active polymer have a high efficiency, good colour stability, and high brightness.
the white-light-emitting devices with phosphorescent dyes are promising for future applications in the display and lighting fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a white-light-emitting device with an active layer can be realized by using a host and a phosphorescent yellow dopant.
the white light emission can be realized by using the phosphorescent dopants.

the phosphorescent dopants with high triplet energy and high quantum efficiency are suitable to be used as the yellow dopants in WPLEDs, and the phosphorescent dyes with a high triplet energy are more effective than fluorescent ones to improve the device efficiency.
